Ana: quick sanity check — copying API_KEY from Secrets Manager, base64-ing with `echo -n` and using Basic auth gives 401. If I paste the already-encoded value into the header it works. any obvious gotchas?

Kevin: do you have the exact curl you used? newline/CRLF from clipboard is the usual suspect. pbpaste/pbcopy on mac can include a trailing newline. try `printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" | base64` instead of `echo`. also check for BOM.

Ana: here's simplified curl I tried:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "apikey:$API_KEY" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/some-endpoint
```
It fails unless I replace the whole header value with the base64 string I copied from the web UI.

Sam: two quick things — 1) if your manager UI is giving you an encoded string maybe it already encodes `apikey:` (so double-encoding can break it). 2) run `printf %s "$API_KEY" | xxd` or `xxd -g 1 -c 16` on the raw value to see trailing 0a/0d or BOM bytes.

Nora: also check language/runtime oddness. node's `Buffer.from(str).toString('base64')` will not strip \r. pwsh will often append \r\n if you use `Get-Clipboard`/`Get-Content` incorrectly. For pwsh encode without newline:
```
$k = Get-Clipboard -Raw
$enc = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($k))
```
That avoids the extra newline.

Kevin: important formatting note for Basic auth: the header must be `Basic <base64(username:password)>`. If you use the API key as the username and an empty password, still include the colon: `echo -n "apikey:" | base64`. Missing the colon changes the bytes and will fail.

Sam: if you want to avoid base64 steps, Redwood accepts Bearer tokens on the Authorization header for API keys: `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY` (if your client supports it). Basic is more error-prone because of the colon/newline traps.

devex-bot: docs: <https://docs.redwood.ai/auth#apikeys> — has a short checklist (no BOM, ensure trailing colon for Basic, prefer Bearer). :mag: 

Ana: tried `printf` + `echo -n 'apikey:' | base64` and `xxd` — found an extra 0d at the end. `tr -d '\r'` fixed it and curl succeeded. thanks all :thumbsup:

Kevin: nice — for scripts use `tr -d '\r\n'` or `sed 's/[\r\n]*$//'` for portability. also consider storing key in a file and doing `-H "Authorization: Basic $(base64 -w0 keyfile)"` so tools don't mangle clipboard.

Nora: if you're debugging streaming clients, add a small test that prints the header bytes before sending — saved me a lot.

Ana: saved — will update the quickstart note in our repo with the `printf` + `base64` snippet and a one-liner test.
